topic: How the Sun makes energy: nuclear fusion
title: Why does the Sun shine? ☀️
hook: Why does the Sun shine, and where does all that energy come from?

scenes.narration: Why does the Sun shine, and where does all that energy come from?
At its center, the core, the temperature reaches about fifteen million degrees Celsius.
There, hydrogen nuclei smash together so hard they fuse into helium, releasing enormous energy.
Every second, the Sun turns about four million tons of its matter into pure energy.
That energy reaches the surface, which is about five thousand five hundred degrees, with cooler dark spots.
From there, sunlight takes about eight minutes to reach Earth.
The Sun is about four point six billion years old, and it has fuel for about five billion more.
In the end it will swell up into a red giant.
And the craziest part: the energy leaving the Sun today may have spent tens of thousands of years bouncing around inside it before escaping.
Send this to someone who brightens your day.

description: In the Sun's core, at about 15 million degrees, hydrogen fuses into helium and releases energy; every second it turns about 4 million tons of matter into energy. The surface is about 5,500 °C and its light takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth, though the energy can take tens of thousands of years to escape the interior. It's about 4.6 billion years old, has about 5 billion to go and will end as a red giant. Original 3D animation; not to scale.

claims.statement: The Sun's core temperature is about 15 million °C.
The Sun converts about 4 million tons of matter into energy every second.
Sunlight takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth.
The Sun is about 4.6 billion years old with about 5 billion years left in its current stage.
Energy made in the core takes tens to hundreds of thousands of years to cross the radiative zone.
